transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Appreciate you making time, Omar. I'd love to start with what's driving the evaluation on your side.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: We're drowning in manual reconciliation between our order system and the warehouse tooling. My team loses maybe fifteen hours a week to it.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: That's the exact shape of problem we built the sync engine for. Can I show you how the field mapping works?

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: This is honestly better than what I sketched for the internal build. What does implementation look like?

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Typical rollout is four to six weeks. We'd pair one of our solutions engineers with your team.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Budget isn't mine to sign off past fifty K, so finance will need to be in the loop at some point. But I want to move this forward.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Send me something I can forward internally. I'll set up a proper demo with a couple more people.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll send a recap today and we'll get the demo on the calendar.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Quick one from me. I floated this upstairs and got a cautious green light to evaluate properly.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Great. Who should be in the room for the full demo?

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Me, probably Nina from the business analysis side, and I want our CFO Rhea there. If she's not bought in early, nothing gets signed at this size.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Understood. I'll build the demo around the cost story as much as the tech.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Second week of March works. I'll get it scheduled on our side.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Looking forward to it. Anything you want me to prep for Rhea specifically?

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Numbers. She will not care about the field mapper. She'll care what it costs and what it saves.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. Omar suggested we spend as much time on the business case as the product, so that's the plan.

transcript.speaker: Rhea Kim
transcript.text: Good, because that's the part I'm here for. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Here's the sync engine running against a copy of a typical order flow. What used to be a manual reconciliation pass just happens continuously.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: For context, this is the fifteen hours a week I keep complaining about.

transcript.speaker: Nina Park
transcript.text: Does the audit trail export? We report on reconciliation exceptions quarterly.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Yes, full export on any window, CSV or straight to your BI tool.

transcript.speaker: Rhea Kim
transcript.text: Before we go further. What does this look like at 500 seats? I need total cost, not list price. Implementation, support tier, the real number.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Fair question. Rather than hand-wave it now, let me put together a full ROI breakdown, real cost against the hours you're losing. I can have that to you this week.

transcript.speaker: Rhea Kim
transcript.text: That works. I want it before we talk again. We start renewal planning for our other vendors in April and this either fits in that cycle or waits a year.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Understood, that timeline is very doable.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: One thing on the technical side. Priya's team will want to see the SSO flow before we sign anything. She runs engineering and she's strict about auth.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Happy to run a session with her team whenever. We're SAML and OIDC out of the box.

transcript.speaker: Rhea Kim
transcript.text: What's your pricing model when seats fluctuate? We're seasonal. I don't want to pay January rates for July headcount.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: There's a flex band on the enterprise tier. I'll make sure the breakdown models your seasonality.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: I'd like to get a sandbox going with our real schemas next.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: I'll have Sam set that up this week.

transcript.speaker: Rhea Kim
transcript.text: Good session. Send me that breakdown and we'll go from there.

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: So the sandbox has your real order schemas loaded. Want to walk through the exception flow?

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: This is exactly what my team needs. The dedupe behavior alone saves us a hire.

transcript.speaker: Nina Park
transcript.text: What export formats does the exception report support? We're a Tableau shop.

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: Native Tableau connector, or CSV if you want raw.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Next step on our side is the security questionnaire. I'll get it over to you this week.

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: Send it whenever. Our compliance docs are ready to go.

transcript.speaker: Omar Diaz
transcript.text: Good. I'm pushing to get this wrapped this month.
